title: PowerShell analyzer surface over the pinned real corpora
method: Candidates are each corpus's production (non-test) tracked .ps1/.psm1/.psd1 files, drawn by a hash of `repo/relative-path` so the sample is unbiased and reproducible; the digest is recorded so a re-run that drew a different set says so instead of being compared. Every file goes through the production `parseFile`. `parseDamage` is measured with a separate parser and is the GRAMMAR's number, independent of any analyzer decision. `lineNumber` counts relationships carrying a positive line. `unknownTargets` counts ONLY the kinds whose both ends are locally declared by definition — `contains`, `overrides`, `extends`, `implements` — whose target matches no symbol in the same file. `calls`, `uses` and `instantiates` are excluded because a cmdlet is an external command and a `uses` edge may name a .NET member; including them made the first run report 3,604 of 9,485 rows, which measured nothing. `dupKeys` counts (file, owner, name, kind) tuples emitted more than once. The owner IS part of the key: a local declared in two functions is two correct declarations, and a proxy that omits the owner reported 186 rows in the first run that were all of that shape. `reservedTargets` uses the reserved set owned by powershell-keyword-census.ts, and skips member-call edges.
limits: This is NOT a truth oracle. It measures what the analyzer emits and how it changed; whether each edge is CORRECT is F5's question, and the powershell lane has no F5 lane. Everything here can be green with every edge wrong, and the completion matrix says so by leaving `diff` and `sharp` as `n/a`.

`unknownTargets` is a proxy for resolvability, not for correctness: a cmdlet target is external by design and is excluded by kind, but a target that names a real cmdlet which happens to share a spelling with a local symbol would be counted as resolved.
Parse damage is the vendored grammar's, and 16 of the powershell corpus's production files plus 15 of ansible's do not parse. Nothing in this instrument attributes that to the analyzer or excuses it.
